title: Tone grilling, round 2: a mood framework
description: Your ask of 19 Nov 2026: a framework, like the Hero's Journey, for how each part of a story carries the mood.
intro: Your words: "I think we need a Framework (like heroes journey) on how each part inside a story carry the mood".
Card 1 checks my reading of your top passages. Cards 2 to 6 shape the framework. No pick from Claude.

sections.title: What your top passages do
sections.sub: Three stories you scored high in the taste tests, each part with its mood (my reading).

cards.title: Is this how your top-scored stories move?
rows: Crowd cheers (high). He ran the wrong way, on national TV (drop). Shame, the worst moment of his life (low). His own line at halftime: a choice (turn). His best football and the win (rise). Talks, letters, a better person (widen). One line for the reader (land).

Parents worship a three-year-old (high). He misses one preschool and they go cold (drop). A failure at three (low, almost absurd). One line names it: failure as who you are (lesson). Dweck: as a kid, I feared that too (me too). A golfer, then rejection letters (widen to the reader).

Last day of school (calm). Hit in the face, told through the body (shock). The slow walk, nobody knew every minute mattered (unease). The nurse's questions, ten seconds to name his mom (creeping dread).
options: Yes, that is how they move
Partly (say what is off in the note)

sections.title: The framework
sections.sub: What it covers, whose mood it tracks, and what it starts from.

cards.title: What counts as "a story" for this framework?
options: a. One told story (David's case, Bayu's drawer)
d. Nested: one shape that works at every level

cards.title: Whose mood does it track?
options: b. The person in the story's

cards.title: Which existing framework is closest to how you feel a story should move?
rows: 12 stages: leave home, the ordeal, return changed. Built for one hero's long journey.
8 steps, a short Hero's Journey: need, go, find, pay, return, changed. Built for short episodes.
4 parts: set up, develop, twist, bring together. No conflict needed. Built in Chinese and Japanese poems and comics.
Moves back and forth between what is and what could be, then ends on the new life. Built for talks that persuade.
Attention, need, answer, picture it, act. Built for speeches that ask for action.
Built from your top passages (card 1) and your own stories.
options: g. A mix, or none of these (say which in the note)

cards.title: Each part gets a mood from your round 1 answers. Use this list?
cards.context: Warm (often). Sure and decisive (often). Curious and amused (often). Playful and self-aware (sometimes). Talking to yourself (sometimes). Blunt (flagships only). Plus new moods you find while writing.
options: Change it (say how in the note)

cards.title: How strict is the framework?
options: a. A fixed order every story follows
b. A usual order, and parts can be skipped or swapped
c. A map used only to check a draft after it is written
